http_route_table.layout: {cstr* path, fn* handler, u32 aux0, u32 aux1, u32 aux2, u32 aux3, u32 aux4}
http_route_table.description: Top-level HTTP route registration: native diagnostic endpoints + UPnP catch-alls. All 23 SOAP /Control paths dispatch to the unified handler f_105e8274 (which then does service+action dispatch via the impl-vtable layer); all /Event paths dispatch to GENA subscribe handler f_105e8290.
http_route_table.event_handler_semantics: f_105e8290 = GENA SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE handler: reads headers NT, NTS, content-length, SID, SEQ via f_100a49ac header-lookup; requires NT==upnp:event and NTS==upnp:propchange else 412 (0x19c); missing headers -> 400 (0x190); method check *(r31)==0xa -> 405 (0x195); valid subscription -> singleton at 0x11097680 v[+0x3c] (subscription manager register call)
http_route_table.control_handler_note: f_105e8274 loads r3=*(0x11097680) singleton then tails into the SOAP engine (service+action dispatch); same subscription/engine singleton as the GENA path

soap_engine.semantics: SOAP engine entry. (1) reads SOAPACTION header via f_100a49ac; (2) f_10c3befc splits it into two 0x80-bounded parts; (3) f_10730c3c constructs the request object from http_req + action parts; (4) x-sonos-target-udn header gate: if present and != local UDN, logs 'unexpected inbound UPnP for UDN=%s method=%s from=%s:%d' and replies 412 (0x19c) via response v[+0x18]; (5) insecureUpnpAllowed settings-key check via f_105580ac; (6) per-dispatch timing log 'UPnP dispatch %s:%s took %u ms'

evidence.notes: engine head: soapaction lookup + split + req build; 0x10693958 x-sonos-target-udn gate; 0x10693d84 insecureUpnpAllowed; 0x10693d60 timing log

request_vtable.0x1c: get REQUIRED in-arg record by name (missing -> parse failure path)
request_vtable.0x20: get OPTIONAL in-arg record by name (absent tolerated, returns null/empty) - vs +0x1c required-lookup
request_vtable.0x3c: arg-binding/parse step (called before +0x08 validate in wrapper f_10732ed8: v[+0x3c] then v[+0x08]->bool then v[+0x14] fault 402)
request_vtable.evidence_note: slot usage measured per-arg in SystemProperties handlers: account credential/metadata fields consistently use +0x20 (optional) while identity fields use +0x1c (required); confirmed again by generated parse f_10731f28: AccountType via +0x1c, AccountID+AccountPassword via +0x20 (both layers)
request_vtable.architecture: Two-layer model: (1) generic request object created by the SOAP engine carries the engine vtable (arg-record lookups at +0x1c/+0x20/+0x24, commit +0x0c, fault +0x14, finalize +0x38). (2) Per-action specialized req-classes (e.g. vtable 0x10f110a8 for AddAccountX) installed by impl vfuncs via stw vptr (e.g. f_10732e94); their generated parse methods (e.g. f_10731f28) call the generic layer's +0x1c/+0x20 by arg name - semantics consistent across both layers. Actions without specialized req-classes (e.g. RegisterMobileDevice via f_10732ebc) call the generic +0x0c execute directly -> no per-arg presence checks.

generic_vtable.req_layout: {+0 vptr, +4 http_req, +8 service-part, +0xc action-part, +0x10 u16 flag, +0x14 in-arg doc, +0x680 out-arg doc}

slots.+0x0c: f_10730850 (commit success response: serialize out-doc via writer vtable 0x10f10f70 at req+0x680; set CONTENT-LENGTH, CONTENT-TYPE text/xml; charset=utf-8, EXT; status 200 via f_100b4614; send f_100b4364; log 'UPnP call: %s:%s returned 200 to %s:%d')
slots.+0x14: f_10731560 (raise fault: sth code->req+0x10; log 'UPnP call: %s:%s returned %d to %s:%d' at level 8 if code>=1000 else 4)
slots.+0x38: f_10731650 (lhz req+0x10 = return stored status/fault code)

generic_vtable.note: All 18 slots resolve to real f_1073* functions. Specialized per-action classes (e.g. AddAccountX 0x10f110a8) subclass this; the ctor f_10730c3c logs 'UPnP call: %s:%s from %s:%d' (category 'upnp') when f_10730bc4(action)!=0xb

evidence.notes: vptr installed at 0x10730c80; layout from store offsets in ctor

generic_vtable.call_log_suppression: ctor f_10730c3c calls f_10730bc4(action) which walks the runtime {name,level} list at 0x110927c0 (seeded with 'ReportUnresponsiveDevice'); index <0xb suppresses the 'UPnP call: %s:%s from %s:%d' log line
generic_vtable.+0x3c_note: f_10730a64: if global *(0x110927bc)!=0, tails f_100a7eac(*(http+0x70)+8) — a peer/debug hook; else no-op

RemoveTrackFromQueue.description: Removes a single track from the queue. Impl f_102aa770: after the 718-gate it fetches the queue's current update-id via f_10149b24(session+0x2d890). A nonzero UpdateID argument must equal that current id or the action returns 0x404 (decimal 1028) — optimistic concurrency; UpdateID=0 skips the check. Mode impl+0x4654 must be 1 or 2 (else 800). It then builds a request record via f_1032e270, tags it with f_1032e440(rec,1,ObjectID), and submits via f_10255f64(session). Submission returns nonzero on success: on success it probes impl+0x5dc via f_1014708c and may clear impl+0x6ed8, returning 0; on submission failure it returns 800.

Unit.description: Seek-mode token; the engine compares it with strcmp against a fixed set and interprets Target accordingly.

special_values.TRACK_NR: target is a queue/track ordinal; only reached when engine mode field (this+0x4654) == 2 and capability bit 0x400000 is set, else 701
special_values.REL_TIME: target is an absolute time position (H:M:S); in stream mode always allowed, in indexed mode requires capability bit 0x200000; negative target rejected with 711 in indexed mode

Target.description: Destination operand whose syntax depends on Unit: a decimal track ordinal for TRACK_NR, or a [-]H:M:S time for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA.
Target.format: TRACK_NR: strtol(Target,NULL,10) on the raw text - base 10, leading whitespace and a +/- sign accepted per strtoul rules, NO endptr so trailing junk is silently ignored ('5junk' -> track 5), saturates at LONG_MIN/MAX on overflow. REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: f_102ab830 consumes at most one leading '-' manually (sets a separate sign flag byte), then sscanf('%hhu:%hhu:%hhu') must return exactly 3. Each %hhu field skips leading whitespace and accepts its own optional +/- sign (strtoul semantics: '-5' wraps to 251); the ':' separators must match literally with no intervening whitespace; each component is stored as u8 so values above 255 wrap mod 256 ('256:00:00' -> 0:00:00, '999' -> 231); trailing characters after the third field are ignored.
Target.accepted_values: TRACK_NR: textual decimal whose strtol result lies in 1..65534. REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: three u8-wrapping decimal components; computed value = h*3600+m*60+s seconds.

range.min: TRACK_NR: 1 (lexical, on unmasked strtol result); REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: 0 s
range.max: TRACK_NR: 65534; REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: 934575 s (255:255:255, components wrap mod 256)

special_values.TRACK_NR text beyond 1..65534 (incl. '0': rejected with 711: validation is (strtol_result - 1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned on the UNMASKED value; the u16 truncation (rlwinm r4,r30,0,16,31 at 0x102b938c) only sizes the record field and never rescues an out-of-range text - '65537' faults, it does not wrap to track 1
special_values.TRACK_NR with trailing junk, leading whi: accepted - strtol skips ws/sign and endptr is NULL so the tail is ignored
special_values.'--H:M:S' or signed components ('-5:00:0: accepted: the outer '-' is consumed manually, then each %hhu applies strtoul sign/wrap rules, so '--0:1:0' parses as negative-(251:00:00 wrapped) - a quirk of layering the manual sign over %hhu
special_values.'00:00:00' or '-00:00:00' (REL_TIME/TIME: zero magnitude -> success WITHOUT submitting any request (0x102b92d4-0x102b9318); '-00:00:00' under REL_TIME still faults 711 because the sign check precedes the zero check
special_values.'-H:M:S' (REL_TIME, indexed mode): rejected with 711 - sign flag byte nonzero and Unit != TIME_DELTA (0x102b9258-0x102b9270)
special_values.'-H:M:S' (TIME_DELTA, indexed mode): accepted; parser negates only the low seconds word (neg at 0x102ab920, hi word stays 0) plus a separate sign byte; submitted as a negative relative offset
special_values.'-H:M:S' (stream mode): not sign-checked at all - the negated seconds word *1000 yields a negative millisecond operand passed straight to the session vfunc; outcome is downstream-determined
special_values.'256:00:00' / '999:99:99' (either mode): accepted with u8 wraparound: 256->0, 999->231 etc.; there is no upper bound check on the total
special_values.'1 :2:3' (whitespace before a colon): rejected - the ':' literals in the scanf format must match immediately
special_values.'01:02:03junk': accepted - sscanf stops after the 3rd conversion and the tail is never inspected

Target.validation: TRACK_NR (indexed mode only): strtol result must satisfy (t-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned else 711; on success u16 field t&0xffff is recorded in the rchsrcreq tag-8 record (the truncation is field-width only; the range check ran on the raw strtol value, so no wrap-to-valid exists). REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: f_102ab830 failure -> 711 indexed / 701 stream; indexed-mode leading '-' under REL_TIME -> 711; indexed-mode zero magnitude -> silent success no-op; stream mode performs no sign or zero gating. Missing/unparsable at the request layer -> 402.

evidence.notes: f_102ab830 Target parser: optional '-' then sscanf '%hhu:%hhu:%hhu', requires 3 fields, computes h*3600+m*60+s i64
bound check: cmplwi (t-1) vs 0xFFFD; u16 t&0xffff stored via rlwinm 0,16,31 at 0x102b938c into rchsrcreq tag-8 record
rlwinm r4,r30,0,16,31 computes the u16 record field from raw strtol result r30; the following addi r30,-1 + cmplwi 0xFFFD at 0x102b9394-0x102b939c validate the UNMASKED value
parser: secs = h*60+m then *60+s via shift/subf; bc on cr4.eq (first char '-') -> neg r7 at 0x102ab920; out pair {secs_word, 0} + separate sign byte at *arg2

Target.notes: Track normalization: strtol -> record field = value & 0xffff -> range check on the RAW value (raw-1 <= 0xFFFD). Ordering means the stored u16 equals the input for every accepted value; masking cannot wrap an out-of-range ordinal into range.

Seek.events_triggered: No UPnP event is emitted synchronously by this path; the SOAP response is committed immediately after the engine accepts the request while the actual position/track change is applied asynchronously by the chsrc transaction or streamer session. Any LastChange/state-variable update therefore originates downstream of the async apply and is not statically proven in this path.
Seek.state_transitions: None synchronously. The accepted seek is queued/applied by the player engine after the call returns; decoder, position and track-index state change happen inside the async transaction/streamer path, not in this handler.
Seek.return_behavior: The impl returns an integer status. On 0 the wrapper commits an empty 200 OK via req vfunc +0x0c (0x102f9494). On nonzero the code is forwarded to the request fault path req vfunc +0x14 at 0x102f944c and surfaces as the UPnPError errorCode. Caveats: (1) the wrapper tests cr0 rather than r3 at 0x102f9440; impl epilogues' stack-canary xor. leaves cr0.eq=1 on normal return, so rc reaches the completion vfunc +0x0c with r4=rc which handles the status-bearing response - the +0x14 branch is effectively a fallback. (2) In stream mode rc==0 only proves a session object accepted the call; the session vfunc's byte result is captured to a flag that gates a log line (0x102b91d8) and is not reflected in the SOAP status - a rejected streamer seek still reports success. (3) In indexed mode rc==0 only proves the rchsrcreq was enqueued, not that the seek applied; a zero-magnitude time target returns 0 without enqueueing at all.

In mode 2 it calls worker f_102af1c8(engine, NextURI, NextURIMetaData), which stores the URI into the next-track record at impl+0x6edc/0x6ee0 (f_106faeb8), manages pending flags impl+0x754c/+0x75cd (cleared) and impl+0x764e (set), fetches the current source URI via f_10293270(impl+0x5dc) and compares it against the engine source name impl+0x3dc: when they differ, the URI is forwarded through the member/topology path (member obj impl+0x448 -> f_10765a00/f_10762c30/f_106fbef4, with "lookup of %s URIs for %s failed" topology logging on failure) — i.e. the next-track request can be delegated to the actual playback member.

Two engine classes implement every action: standalone (vtable 0x10eaf2ec, ctor f_102cc070) and group-capable (vtable 0x10edfbb8, ctor f_104000c4). They share all 54 vfunc slots except ctor/dtor and the four coordinator-sensitive impls (+0x08 SetAVTransportURI, +0x54 BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup, +0xd0 BecomeGroupCoordinator, +0xd4 BecomeGroupCoordinatorAndSource). All four playlist-format workers share one skeleton: playlist log tag + iterateXxxPlayList %s, fetch through the stream abstraction (f_10545064 open / f_10546520 read / f_1054103c close), per-entry job submission on shared delegate machinery. /MediaRenderer/RenderingControl/Control.name: RenderingControl
/MediaRenderer/RenderingControl/Control.description: UPnP RenderingControl for the zone player: per-channel volume, mute, loudness and EQ state held in a large implementation object (fields through at least +0x9c8) guarded by a recursive mutex at impl+0x938. Two implementation classes share the same SOAP vtable layout: a base 'without proxy' class (vtable 0x10e872f0, methods 0x100dxxxx-0x100exxxx, e.g. SetMute logs 'SetMuteWithoutProxy') and a derived class (vtable 0x10ed279c, overrides at 0x1046xxxx) that performs a grouped-operation prelude (object built from impl+0xbc8 and impl+0x9c8 via f_1046dff0, submitted via f_1046c3cc) before tail-calling the base implementation - i.e. the proxy/grouped variant. Which class is installed at *(svc+4) is decided at rc_impl construction (selection condition unresolved); several actions are 3-instruction null stubs in one or both classes and are documented per-class below.

0x105cd004.assessment: NOT a SOAP dispatcher. Compares an HTTP response line against 'HTTP/1.1 401' and 'HTTP/1.0 401' (strncmp n=0xc at 0x105cd030/0x105cd04c); on match writes literal 0x191 into *(ctx+0x10000-0x7a94) and calls f_1056c310; otherwise falls through to f_10541494 (header/body parse). This is the HTTP client stack's 401-response detector — no service binding. Literals: HTTP/1.1 401 / HTTP/1.0 401 + WWW-Authenticate: header parse + text/json -> outbound HTTP client auth-failure/negotiation path (cloud API client), not a dispatcher.

0x10651eec.assessment: NOT a SOAP dispatcher — a native HTTP endpoint. Looks up request header 'x-rincon-content-format' (f_100a49ac), paranoid_atoui parses it, then indexes a handler table at r28+4+4*r29 and calls the selected object's v[+0x08]; bad/missing handler emits 401 via f_100b4614+f_100b4364. Part of the rincon HTTP API surface (binary PUT/POST endpoints), not UPnP SOAP. Endpoint subsystem identified via in-body literals: x-rincon-content-format header + repset + RINCON_FFFFFFFFFFFF99999 + informLocalReplicatedSettingVersion/ReplicatedSettingsChangedEvent logs -> household replicated-settings (repset) HTTP endpoint serving text/xml.

0x1068e65c.assessment: NOT a SOAP dispatcher — native binary protocol handler. Parses a TLV-ish record via f_109dd184, reads tag byte at buf+2 and u16 at buf+0, f_109e10d8 maps to a command id (compared 0x4a), calls f_1067c700 worker; result stored at r31+0x30 with a 0x34-length path. Same TLV helper family as 0x1068e904/0x1068ec54 — a non-SOAP native protocol surface (SCI/netstart/zone-bus candidate). Body literals identify the surface: Invalid transport: WSS is required / Invalid namespace: UPnP renew not supported / Invalid namespace: UPnP unsubscribe not supported -> websocket (WSS) eventing handler carrying a binary/TLV-framed command set (cmd 0x4a seen); UPnP-style SUBSCRIBE/RENEW/UNSUBSCRIBE namespaces rejected by name.

0x1068e904.assessment: NOT a SOAP dispatcher — native binary protocol handler sharing the f_109dd184/f_109e10d8 TLV helpers with 0x1068e65c; additionally f_109dcb6c + inet_aton parse a dotted-quad field out of the TLV record (0x1068e9a0-0x1068e9ac) — an address-bearing network-config command handler. Same WSS/TLV surface as 0x1068e65c plus an http:// and inet_aton dotted-quad field -> address-bearing subscribe/register message variant.

0x1068ec54.assessment: NOT a SOAP dispatcher — large native protocol worker operating on a message object at r31 with fields +0xec/+0xf0/+0xf4/+0x108/+0x10c; copies spans via f_1068c040 into stack frames. Part of the same non-SOAP binary surface as 0x1068e65c/0x1068e904. Same WSS binary surface; worker on the message object (fields +0xec/+0xf0/+0xf4/+0x108/+0x10c).

0x106bb20c.assessment: NOT a SOAP dispatcher — a name-keyed property dispatcher. Reads a key name at *(r5)+0, strcmp's it against 'explicitContentFiltering' (0x106bb274), gates on an object vfunc (*(r4+8)->*; cmplwi 0x12b at 0x106bb288), then calls builder f_106ba850. A config/property set path (explicit-content-filtering toggle), not a UPnP action. Literals: explicitContentFiltering key (x2), Access token is too old, Unsupported Request, text/plain responses, MemFree:/MemAvailable: debug fields -> native config-key HTTP endpoint (parental-control + device-info keys), not SOAP.

0x1073d8f8.assessment: RESOLVED: dispatcher 0x1073d8f8 is the AudioIn service dispatcher (vtable 0x10f11f70 at svc+0, installed by ctor f_1073d930 into *(r3-in+0xaa6c)). Reject-all: emits 401 for every action — the service is a registered stub in this build.

SonosSeekTime.description: Sonos time-position operand produced by f_102ab830: an optional leading '-' sets a separate sign flag, then sscanf('%hhu:%hhu:%hhu') must convert exactly three decimal fields. Each %hhu applies strtoul semantics per component - leading whitespace skipped, own optional +/- sign allowed, result truncated to u8 so >255 wraps mod 256. The ':' separators match literally (no whitespace before them); trailing characters after the third field are ignored. Output is a {seconds_word, fraction_word=0} pair (printed as '%lld.%06lld') plus the sign byte; a leading '-' negates only the seconds word. Total range 0..934575 s (255:255:255); there is no upper-bound check.
SonosSeekTime.format: [-]H:M:S where each component is a scanf %hhu (u8, mod-256 wrap); exactly three required; trailing junk ignored
used_by: AVTransport.Seek (Target for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA, both indexed and stream modes)

evidence.notes: sign skip via cmplwi '-' + r3+=cr4.eq; sscanf fmt at 0x10eafc7c; secs=(h*60+m)*60+s; neg on cr4.eq; stw {secs,0} pair + sign byte

SonosSeekTime.notes: Action-specific restrictions layer on top: e.g. Seek indexed mode rejects a set sign flag unless Unit==TIME_DELTA, and treats a zero-magnitude pair as a silent no-op success. Stream mode performs no sign or zero gating.

SonosTrackOrdinal.description: Sonos track-ordinal operand: strtol(text,NULL,10) on the raw string - base 10, leading whitespace and +/- accepted, endptr NULL so trailing junk is silently ignored ('5junk' -> 5), saturates at LONG_MIN/MAX. Acceptance range is validated on the UNMASKED strtol result as (value-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned, i.e. exactly 1..65534; a separate u16 truncation (value & 0xffff) sizes the downstream record field and cannot wrap an out-of-range input into validity.
SonosTrackOrdinal.format: decimal integer, strtol base 10; accepted lexical range 1..65534

evidence.notes: strtol(r26,0,10); rlwinm &0xffff at 0x102b938c sizes the record field; addi r30,-1 + cmplwi 0xFFFD at 0x102b9394-0x102b939c validates the raw value

SonosTrackOrdinal.notes: The mask-before-validate ordering looks alarming but is inert: the record field is computed pre-check, the check uses the raw value, and a rejected record is destroyed unsubmitted.

queue_engine_object.description: Queue engine object held at *(queue-manager+0x128). Three Queue impl forwarders (AddMultipleURIs 0x1046594c, ReplaceAllTracks 0x10465970, SaveAsSonosPlaylist 0x10465f94) dispatch through its vtable at slots +0xd8/+0xdc/+0x7c. The other six mutations call queue-manager methods directly (f_102b6948 AddURI, f_102b2da4 AttachQueue, f_102dff24 CreateQueue {0,402}, f_102b3a84 RemoveAllTracks {718,1028,derived}, f_102b3954 ReorderTracks-gate 402, f_102b3924 variants). Queue svc object ctor f_104656d0 installs vptr 0x10ed19a8 only; the engine member is injected by later init wiring. Engine worker f_102b62e8 (281 insns, single exit): per-item URI-insertion aggregator — iterates item descriptors, calls f_10255f64(*(obj+0x580), doc) per item (queue-store insert), writes per-item results to caller out-pointers, failure paths seed 800. Domain {0,800}; called by f_102b674c, f_102b6b04(x2), f_102d8518, f_102dac20 (AVT queue-mutation family). *(obj+0x4654) state counter gates entry (same member SaveQueue checks for its 800 path). Host structure resolved: the queue manager is a member of the zone-player composite object (r16 in ctor f_1018d27c), which embeds ~30 interface sub-objects at stride 0x20 starting +0x124 — each: vptr + self-member. Master vtable-install block at 0x1018da20-0x1018db50 loads secondary vtables from group 0x10e97d5c (+0x31c..+0x810): +0x124->0x10e98098, +0x144->0x10e980b0, +0x164->0x10e980c8 etc. Each secondary vtable ~4 slots {2 methods + dtor pair f_10192fXX/f_10193XXX + vbase-offset word}. *(manager+0x128) self-points to manager+0x130 (nested member), so the engine dispatch goes through the sub-object at manager+0x124 (vtable 0x10e98098: f_10187d14, f_100e5628, f_10192f90, f_10193148). Layout correction: the zone-player composite (r16) carries TWO vptr families — (a) primary bank at 0x10e979e0 installed at r16+0xc plus 9 secondary bases at stride 0x1c (r16+0x28..+0x108, vtables 0x10e979f0..0x10e97a70 stride 0x10 = 4 slots each), and (b) the earlier 0x20-stride chain (vtable group 0x10e97d5c). r16+0x108 sub-object vptr = 0x10e979d0 with first member ptr to r16+0x114. The queue svc impl reads *(r3+0x128); if the queue base is one of these embedded bases, +0x128 lands inside the following 0x20-chain region — the engine is the sub-object whose vptr is installed there (vtable-identity still unresolved; the +0x128 read is a member ptr, not the vptr itself). f_1018069c identified as the shared_ptr control-block attach helper (subf distance<=15 check, lwsync barrier) — the 0x20-stride chain blocks are shared_ptr {px,pn} handles, each bound to the adjacent sub-object. So *(svc+0x128) reads a shared_ptr px member pointing into the neighbouring embedded object; the queue engine itself is a heap/nested object reached through that handle, consistent with runtime wiring. Engine vfunc table remains unresolved.
